text:
vanya: Heads-up — seeing a p95 east-west latency spike during the 11:30–12:00 batch ramp in us-west-2. Started ~11:34, affects inference lanes on two racks. @alex can you triage? :thinking_face:

alex: On it. Graphs (RPC latency) jump from ~2ms -> ~85ms for inter-node calls. Local rack traffic looks ok. Any ToR errors?

infra-bot: autoscaler: added 12 nodes to us-west-2 during 11:31–11:35 (policy: batch-ramp-scale)

maria: worth checking KV cache warmup thrash — batch sizes doubled around same time. Could be bursty east-west fanout + autoscale churn.

noah: starting quick nets tests. Running iperf3 between gpu-node-a (rack1) -> gpu-node-b (same rack) and cross-rack to gpu-node-c

noah: command: `iperf3 -c gpu-node-b -t 10 -R`

noah: iperf3 output (same-rack):
```
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bitrate
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  1.05 GBytes   902 Mbits/sec
```

noah: cross-rack to gpu-node-c: 200–300 Mbps, high retransmits and jitter (~30ms spikes)

alex: ran `ethtool -S eth0` on the affected pair — rx_dropped is climbing in the 11:33–11:35 window:
```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_errors|rx_dropped|tx_errors'
rx_dropped: 12345
tx_errors: 0
```

maria: rdma counters look nominal on the NIC side, but we're using host-gw CNI so ARP and routing churn when new nodes join could produce microbursts. Also autoscaler adding nodes may have pushed a large reshuffle of shards.

sam: checked ToR logs — spine-3 port Gi1/45 flapped at 11:33:12 for ~9s, then cleared. Vendor reported CRC increments on that port.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0221 created (severity P1) — tagging networking, infra, and colo teams.

vanya: immediate plan: 1) isolate batch traffic to rack-local pools where possible, 2) rollback the aggressive autoscale cooldown, 3) collect tc and pcap on affected nodes.

alex: opening runbook (link) and starting packet captures on the affected nodes: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/ew-spike.pcap 'tcp'` — started 11:36. Also running `tc -s qdisc` to check queue drops.

maria: lowering batching window and backoff to reduce inter-node burst for the next hour — deploying conservative policy now.

noah: quick `ethtool -S` diff shows rx_crc_errors incrementing on spine-3 interface toward rack-2. Starting `ibv_rc_pingpong` just to sanity-check RDMA path (results nominal).

vanya: if ToR flaps persist we'll request SFP swap from colo and move critical lanes to alternate spine. Can we route new batch lanes to rack-local nodes temporarily?

alex: yes — re-routing policy applied for lanes 3/4 to prefer rack-local pools. Also adding a 30s cooldown to autoscaler (PR merged).

sam: colo NOC replied — they also see CRC errors on the SFP reported by spine-3. Replacement SFPs inbound, ETA 37m.

maria: capture saved to /tmp/ew-spike.pcap and uploaded to infra S3 for deeper analysis. Initial pcap shows bursts of small flows from many new nodes at 11:33.

vanya: thanks. Mitigations: rack-local routing + autoscaler cooldown + SFP replacement in flight. Monitor next hourly batch ramp and update. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INC-2026-0221 severity lowered to P2 — awaiting verification and post-incident capture analysis.
